extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of world history
extracted.subtask_description: An extract from a general-history textbook outlining causes and qualities of state formation, the role of religion and education, and the characteristics of notable rulers (e.g., Akbar) in shaping civilizations. Useful for analyses of political development and cultural consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of education as essential factor
rubrics_metrics.description: "The essential factor in the organization of a living state, the world is coming to realize, is the organization of an education."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells argues that a living/lasting state depends fundamentally on organized education (schools, universities, cheap books). Education is a collective function; without it popular consciousness and a common civic spirit cannot be created or sustained. Examples: Akbar set up schools; the Catholic Church provided popular teaching and universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern state = combination of community of faith and community of will
rubrics_metrics.description: "This modern state ... is a tentative combination of two apparently contradictory ideas, the idea of a community of faith and obedience ... and the idea of a community of will."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The modern state reconciles communal religious/obedience-based cohesion with the participatory, self-reliant 'community of will' of nomadic/traditional polities. Evaluation of a state's 'modernity' can consider how well it balances shared moral/faith foundations with institutions enabling citizen participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information must precede consultation / informed electorate
rubrics_metrics.description: "The modern citizen... must be informed first and then consulted. Before he can vote he must hear the evidence; before he can decide he must know."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Democratic procedures are meaningless without accessible information and education. Practical guidance: prioritize schools, literature, news, and means of communication before expecting effective popular consultation or voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion/ideology as a unifying source of moral education
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is in the fact that both Christianity and Islam ... did at least promise to supply ... a common moral education for a mass of people"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large communities historically have been united by broad religious/ideological systems that provide common history, moral teaching, and identity. Evaluation: measure how an ideology functions as mass pedagogy and links diverse peoples; note both positive unifying effects and the crudeness or limitations of such education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions of popular teaching and intercommunication (church, universities, written word)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Catholic Church provided ... a system of popular teaching, a number of universities and methods of intellectual inter-communication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durable political communities require institutions (schools, universities, written media) that transmit ideas widely. The 'written word' and organized institutions enable the formation of a common public intelligence; assess presence/quality of such institutions when judging state capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness, toleration, and inclusion as marks of effective rulers (Akbar example)
rubrics_metrics.description: "His distinctive quality was his openness of mind... tolerant to men of other beliefs, impartial to men of other races... he set himself to make every sort of able man in India, whatever his race or religion, available for the public work of Indian life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells presents Akbar as exemplary: recruit talented individuals regardless of background; patronize scholarship and cultural translation; practice humane treatment of conquered peoples; hold tolerant policies to weld diverse societies into a common polity. Use these attributes to evaluate leadership effectiveness in multi-ethnic states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-down imposed state-religion without popular roots will fail
rubrics_metrics.description: "This new state religion, however, died with him, because it had no roots in the minds of the people about him."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts to create unity by inventing or imposing a state creed are fragile unless they resonate with the population's beliefs and practices. Assessment: check whether ideological initiatives have grassroots support and institutional embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and orientation of teachers/educational elites matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Moslem teachers in India were not so much teachers as conservators of an intense bigotry... The Brahmins... had all the conceit and slackness of hereditary privilege."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who teaches matters: educators can either foster a common, critical civic mind or entrench sectarianism and inertia. Evaluate curricula, motives of elites, and whether educational systems promote openness or preserve privilege and dogma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of infrastructure and towns is crucial to civilization's survival
rubrics_metrics.description: Wells' account of Hulagu: he "destroyed the irrigation system that had endured for at least eight thousand years, and with that the mother civilization of all the Western world came to an end."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material infrastructure (irrigation, towns, systems of cultivation) underpins civilization; their deliberate destruction causes long-term collapse. Use presence/maintenance of infrastructure as a criterion when assessing societal resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of will limited by community of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "The community of will is limited in size by the limitations set upon the possibilities of a community of knowledge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale of participatory political communities depends on shared knowledge and communication. To evaluate potential for large-scale self-government, measure the reach of education, media, and means for aligning wills (schools, news, common information channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime trade and voyaging promote intellectual freedom and modern growth
rubrics_metrics.description: "It seems as inevitable that voyaging should make men free in their minds as that settlement within a narrow horizon should make men timid and servile."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to trade, travel, and mercantile life fosters openness, initiative, and the growth of towns—factors associated with modernization. Assess impact of shipping/trade networks on cultural and political dynamism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Servile/authoritarian civilizations become vulnerable through social decay
rubrics_metrics.description: Wells' critique of Rome and other servile states: concentration of property and reliance on slaves led to decay and susceptibility to conquest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate social structures: concentration of wealth, decline of public spirit, and erosion of education reduce civic capacity and invite external domination. Indicators: property concentration, slave/dependency systems, decline in public education and civic institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern ideal: an educational government
rubrics_metrics.description: "The modern ideal, the ideal of a world-wide educational government, in which the ordinary man is neither the slave of an absolute monarch nor of a demagogue-ruled state, but an informed, inspired, and consulted part of his community."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wells prescribes a model of governance where the state's role includes organizing education and information access so citizens can be genuinely consulted. When judging modern governance, consider extent to which the state enables universal education, free information, and informed participation rather than only providing formal political rights.
